mainTopic: The lower sign alone makes a girl an adult, and who may check for the signs
overview: The amud opens with the last line of a homiletic reading about stages of breast development. The גמרא then asks where we learn that the lower sign (two hairs) alone makes a girl an adult. It answers from במדבר ה:ו, which treats a woman like a man for punishments: a man becomes an adult with one sign, the lower one, so a woman does too. A ברייתא from יבנה supports this. Several ברייתות follow about which sign or side tends to develop first, depending on a girl's way of life. Next, a ברייתא rules that women do the checking for signs. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree about whether women may check during the age window from eleven to twelve. The ברייתא adds that a woman is believed only to be stringent, shown through cases of מיאון and חליצה. The גמרא explains each opinion, using רבא's presumption that a girl of twelve has grown signs. It ends by asking whose view the stringency rule follows, answering that it may be רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Closing line of a homiletic reading about breast development
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier homiletic reading of a פסוק. It describes two stages of breast development and says that at neither stage did the subject change her ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: When your breasts began to form, you did not change your ways. When your breasts were fully grown, you still did not change your ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a homiletic reading of a פסוק that it started before this section. The reading uses the stages of a girl's breast development as a picture of not doing תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words name two separate stages: first the breasts begin to form, then they are fully grown. This matches the 'upper sign' of adulthood that the surrounding discussion deals with. The point of the reading is the moral rebuke: even as she grew more mature, she did not change.

keyTerms.meaning: Began to form or take shape (the first stage of development)
You turned back, you changed your ways

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the tail end of an earlier homiletic reading. It is not the start of the new legal question, which begins in the next step.

phrases.english: Your breasts began to form — you did not change your ways,

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתְּדוֹ דַּדַּיִךְ — נָמֵי לָא הֲדַרְתְּ בָּךְ.
phrases.english: your breasts became fully grown — you also did not change your ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכְּרַפוּ דַּדַּיִךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a homiletic reading that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two stages of breast development are described, and the subject did not repent at either stage.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the lower sign alone is enough
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that we rely on the lower sign (שתי שערות) to make a girl an adult. The גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, everyone agrees that we rely on the lower sign. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants a source for the rule that the lower sign by itself is enough to make a girl an adult. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier there was a dispute about how much weight the upper sign (breasts) carries. But both sides agree that the lower sign alone counts, even without the upper sign. The גמרא asks why the lower sign is enough on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower sign: two pubic hairs (שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: In any case, according to everyone,
phrases.notes: Everyone here means both sides of the earlier dispute, רבי מאיר and the חכמים.

phrases.english: we rely on the lower sign — from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהָא אַתַּחְתּוֹן סָמְכִינַן, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the homiletic reading to a legal question about the signs of adulthood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for relying on the lower sign alone to make a girl an adult.

steps.title: A woman is compared to a man, so one sign is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב, and also the school of רבי ישמעאל, learn from במדבר ה:ו that the Torah treats a woman like a man for all punishments. A man becomes an adult with one sign, so a woman does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: The פסוק says 'A man or woman, when they commit any of the sins of men.' The Torah made a woman equal to a man for all the punishments in the Torah. Just as a man becomes an adult with one sign, so too a woman becomes an adult with one sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a פסוק that puts men and women side by side. From that comparison it learns that a woman, like a man, needs only one sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being punished requires being an adult. So if a woman is equal to a man for punishments, she should also become an adult the way he does. A man has only one sign of adulthood, so a woman needs only one sign as well, and does not need both the lower and upper signs.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah made them equal (treated them the same)

steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison of a woman to a man is the base that the rest of the section builds on.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said,
and likewise the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
The verse states: “A man or woman,
when they commit any of the sins of men”
the Torah made a woman equal to a man
for all the punishments in the Torah.
Just as a man becomes an adult with one sign,
so too a woman becomes an adult with one sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: במדבר ה:ו makes a woman equal to a man, and a man needs only one sign, so a woman needs only one sign.

steps.title: Maybe a woman's one sign could be either lower or upper
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The comparison shows only that one sign is enough, so maybe a woman could become an adult through either sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: either this sign or that sign!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 3. It says the comparison only proves that she needs one sign, not which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 proved the number of signs (one), not which kind. A woman has two possible signs, the lower one and the upper one (breasts). So maybe either one alone would be enough, and the lower sign would not be special.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (opens another possible reading)
Either this one or that one

phrases.english: But say instead: either this sign or that sign!
phrases.notes: 'This' is the lower sign and 'that' is the upper sign, breast development.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: אוֹ הַאי אוֹ הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how much step 3 actually proves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation 'a woman, like a man, needs one sign'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison sets the number of signs but not which sign, so the upper sign alone might also be enough.

steps.title: Like a man: only the lower sign counts
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to a man also tells us which sign. A man becomes an adult through the lower sign, not an upper one, so the same is true for a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like a man: just as a man becomes an adult through the lower sign and not the upper sign, so too a woman becomes an adult through the lower sign and not the upper sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by using the same comparison more fully. A woman is like a man both in how many signs she needs and in which sign it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man has no upper sign at all. His adulthood comes only from the lower sign. Since a woman is compared to a man, her one sign must also be the lower one, and the upper sign alone does not set her adulthood under this comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower sign, not the upper

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison of a woman to a man (במדבר ה:ו) teaches two things: she needs only one sign, and that sign is the lower one, just like a man.

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִישׁ — מָה אִישׁ תַּחְתּוֹן וְלֹא עֶלְיוֹן,
phrases.english: Like a man — just as a man becomes an adult through the lower sign and not the upper sign,
so too a woman becomes an adult through the lower sign and not the upper sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּאִישׁ — מָה אִישׁ תַּחְתּוֹן וְלֹא עֶלְיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends the same comparison to cover which sign counts, not only how many.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either the lower or the upper sign alone might make a woman an adult.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because a woman is compared to a man, only the lower sign makes her an adult under this comparison.

steps.title: Support from יבנה: once the lower sign appears, the upper sign is ignored
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up this conclusion. רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק reports that in יבנה they said that once the lower sign has appeared, we no longer look at the upper sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק said, this is how they would explain it in יבנה, and they said: once the lower sign has come, we no longer pay attention to the upper sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the rule it just reached. The rule is that the lower sign alone settles a girl's adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sages of יבנה ruled that once the lower sign appears, it does not matter whether the upper sign has appeared. This matches the conclusion from the פסוק that the lower sign is what counts.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also taught in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
Yavne, where the main study hall was after the destruction of the second בית המקדש
We do not pay attention to

steps.whatToRemember: Once the lower sign (שתי שערות) has appeared, a girl is an adult, and we do not need to check the upper sign.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, said:
This is how they would explain it in Yavne, and they said:
Once the lower sign has appeared,
we no longer pay attention to the upper sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports the conclusion of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the lower sign alone makes a girl an adult.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר ברבי צדוק reporting what was said in יבנה.

steps.title: City girls and village girls develop different signs first
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that for city girls the lower sign comes first, and for village girls the upper sign comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: in girls from big cities, the lower sign comes faster because they often go to bathhouses. In girls from villages, the upper sign comes faster because they grind grain with millstones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that a girl's daily life affects which sign of maturity appears first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that only the lower sign makes a girl an adult. This ברייתא adds a practical fact: the two signs do not always come in the same order. City life, with its warm baths, speeds up the hair (lower sign), and the hard work of grinding speeds up chest growth (upper sign).
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is only about which sign shows up first. It does not change the rule from the earlier steps that only the lower sign makes a girl an adult.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Girls from cities:
the lower sign comes more quickly,
phrases.notes: The lower sign is the two hairs, the same sign the earlier steps said makes her an adult.

phrases.english: because they regularly go to bathhouses;
girls from villages:
the upper sign comes more quickly,
phrases.notes: The upper sign means the chest starting to develop.

phrases.english: because they grind with millstones.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling that the lower sign is what counts, the גמרא brings information on the order in which the signs appear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lifestyle decides which sign comes first: bathhouses speed up the lower sign, and grinding speeds up the upper sign.

steps.title: Rich girls and poor girls develop different sides first
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר teaches that among wealthy girls the right side of the chest develops first, and among poor girls the left side develops first. Two reasons are given for the poor girls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: in daughters of the rich, the right side comes faster because it rubs against their fancy cloaks. In daughters of the poor, the left side comes faster because they carry water jugs on that side. Or, if you like, because they carry their younger brothers on their hips.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא adds that daily life also decides which side of the chest develops first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a closer look at the upper sign. Wealthy girls wear a cloak that rubs the right side, so that side grows first. Poor girls carry heavy loads on the left, either water jugs or little brothers, so the left side grows first.

keyTerms.meaning: Their upper cloaks, worn by the wealthy
And if you wish, say: introduces a second possible explanation

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹת עֲשִׁירִים — צַד יָמִין מְמַהֵר לָבֹא,
phrases.english: daughters of the rich: the right side comes more quickly,
phrases.notes: He's talking about the upper sign here, meaning which side of the chest starts growing first.

phrases.english: since it rubs against their cloaks.

phrases.aramaic: בָּנוֹת עֲנִיִּים — צַד שְׂמֹאל מְמַהֵר לָבֹא,
phrases.english: daughters of the poor: the left side comes more quickly,
because they carry jugs of water on it.
And if you wish, say:
because they carry their brothers on their sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of lifestyle affecting development, moving from which sign comes first to which side develops first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Among the rich the right side develops first; among the poor the left side develops first.

steps.title: The left side comes before the right
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that the left side of the chest develops before the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: the left side comes before the right side.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives a general rule that the left side normally develops first. This sets up the disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier step, this is stated as a general rule for all girls, without dividing between rich and poor. The very next step will argue with it.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The left side comes before the right side.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: צַד שְׂמֹאל קוֹדֵם לְצַד יָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a general rule about which side develops first, following the rich and poor distinction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The left side generally develops before the right.

steps.title: From experience: the left side almost never comes first
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אחי רבי יהושע disagrees. From what he has seen, the left side came first only once, in a girl in his neighborhood, and even then the right side later caught up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא, the nephew of רבי יהושע, says: the left side never came before the right, except for one girl in my neighborhood. Her left side came before her right side, and then it went back to normal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא pushes back on the previous ברייתא, using what he has seen himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step said the left side comes first. רבי חנינא says the normal order is the opposite: right before left. He knows of only one exception, and even that girl later developed normally.
steps.whatToRemember: Which side develops first is debated, but all of this concerns only the upper sign. The הלכה from the earlier steps stays the same: the lower sign is what makes a girl an adult.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, son of the brother of Rabbi Yehoshua, says:

phrases.aramaic: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא קָדַם צַד שְׂמֹאל לְצַד יָמִין,
phrases.english: The left side never came before the right side,
except for one girl who was in my neighborhood,
whose left side came before the right side,
and it went back to its normal state.
phrases.notes: He means that her right side later developed normally too.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעוֹלָם לֹא קָדַם צַד שְׂמֹאל לְצַד יָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly disagrees with the ברייתא in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the general claim that the left side comes first.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His experience shows the right side normally comes first; a left-first case is a rare exception that later evened out.

steps.title: Women do the checking for signs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that whenever a girl must be checked for signs of maturity, women do the checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: all girls who need to be checked are checked by women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new practical question: who checks a girl for the signs of maturity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know which sign counts, someone has to check for it. The ברייתא says the checking is done by women, and we rely on their report.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַנִּבְדָּקוֹת נִבְדָּקוֹת עַל פִּי נָשִׁים,
phrases.english: All girls who are checked are checked based on the word of women,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל הַנִּבְדָּקוֹת נִבְדָּקוֹת עַל פִּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from how the signs develop to who examines for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Checking for signs of maturity is done by women, and their report is trusted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical way the earlier halacha is carried out: the court relies on women's testimony about the signs.

steps.title: Great רבנים followed this in practice
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר sent girls to his wife to be checked, and רבי ישמעאל sent them to his mother, which shows the ruling was followed in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so רבי אליעזר would hand the girls over to his wife, and רבי ישמעאל would hand them over to his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up its ruling by showing that two great רבנים actually did this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וכן, meaning 'and so', ties these stories to the rule just stated. Real practice by leading sages shows the rule was not just theory: they trusted the women in their own homes to do the checking.

keyTerms.meaning: And so: introduces practice that matches the rule

steps.whatToRemember: A girl's adulthood depends on the lower sign, and women are the ones who check for it. רבי אליעזר and רבי ישמעאל followed this themselves.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מוֹסֵר לְאִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: And so Rabbi Eliezer would hand them over to his wife,
phrases.notes: He means he gave the girls who needed checking to his wife to examine.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael would hand them over to his mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מוֹסֵר לְאִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule of step 11 with real practice.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that women do the checking for signs.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי אליעזר, who used his wife, and רבי ישמעאל, who used his mother.

steps.title: Women may check before and after the age window, but not during it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that women may check a girl before the age window and after it, but not during it, because doubtful cases are not settled by women's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: before the age window and after it, women check the girls. During the window, women do not check them, because we do not settle doubtful cases based on women.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and brings רבי יהודה, who limits the general rule that women do the checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the window, any hair found does not count as a sign, and after it the girl is assumed to be an adult. During the window, a woman's report could decide a real doubt, and רבי יהודה says doubts are not settled by women.

keyTerms.meaning: The set age window, from eleven years and a day to twelve years and a day, when hair can count as a sign

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Before the age window and after the age window
phrases.notes: "The age window" runs from eleven years and a day to twelve years and a day. That is when hair can count as a sign.

phrases.english: women check them,
during the age window
women do not check them,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מַשִּׂיאִין סְפֵקוֹת עַל פִּי נָשִׁים.
phrases.english: because we do not settle doubtful cases based on women.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לִפְנֵי הַפֶּרֶק וּלְאַחַר הַפֶּרֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's general rule from step 11 that women do the checking
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women may check before and after the age window, but not during it, because doubts are not settled by women.

steps.title: Women may check even during the window, but only to be stringent
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that women may check even during the age window. A woman is believed only when her report leads to a stricter result, not a more lenient one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: even during the age window women check them, and a woman is believed to be stringent but not to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה and lets women check during the window too, with one limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון lets women check even during the window. The line 'a woman is believed to be stringent but not lenient' comes right after his words, so it looks like part of his view. Later (steps 24-25) the גמרא asks whose rule this line really is, and its first answer is רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: To be stringent, leading to a stricter result
To be lenient, leading to a more permissive result

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even during the age window
women check them,
and a woman is believed to be stringent
but not to be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף תּוֹךְ הַפֶּרֶק נָשִׁים בּוֹדְקוֹת אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה in step 13 about checking during the window
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women may check during the window too, but are believed only for stringency.

steps.title: Examples of a woman being believed to be stringent
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that if the woman says the girl is an adult, the girl can no longer do מיאון. If she says the girl is a minor, the girl cannot do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If she says "She is an adult," then the girl may not refuse. If she says "She is a minor," then the girl may not do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks "how so?" and shows what "believed to be stringent" means in real cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each report is used only for the result that closes a door. Calling her an adult takes away מיאון, which only a minor can do. Calling her a minor takes away חליצה, which a minor cannot validly do.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? Asks for a practical example
Refusal: a girl married off as a minor by her mother or brother rejects the marriage, which works only before she is an adult
The ceremony that frees a widow from יבום; it must be done by an adult

steps.confusionAlert: Both reports here are "stringent" even though they are opposites. The woman is believed only for the side of each report that forbids something.

phrases.english: How so?
"She is an adult"
so that she may not refuse,
phrases.notes: Only a minor can do מיאון. Once she is treated as an adult, that option is gone.

phrases.english: "She is a minor"
so that she may not do חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? גְּדוֹלָה הִיא שֶׁלֹּא תְּמָאֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives concrete examples of the rule 'believed to be stringent but not lenient' from step 14. Steps 24-25 discuss whose rule this is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's report of adult or minor is accepted only to block מיאון or חליצה.

steps.title: A woman is not believed to allow מיאון or חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes: the woman is not believed when she says the girl is a minor so that she may refuse, or an adult so that she may do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But she is not believed to say "She is a minor" so that the girl may refuse, or "She is an adult" so that the girl may do חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows the other side of the 'stringent but not lenient' rule: cases where the woman's word would make things more lenient, so it is not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same two statements, "minor" and "adult," are now used to allow an action, and here the woman is not trusted. This finishes the picture of "stringent but not lenient."

keyTerms.meaning: An adult girl (past the age of maturity with signs)

steps.whatToRemember: A woman's check during the age window works only to forbid: it can block מיאון or חליצה, but it can never allow them. The גמרא later (step 25) says this rule can follow רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: But she is not believed to say
"She is a minor" so that she may refuse,
and "She is an adult" so that she may do חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵין נֶאֱמֶנֶת לוֹמַר קְטַנָּה הִיא שֶׁתְּמָאֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 15 by giving the lenient cases where the woman is not believed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman is not believed to allow מיאון or חליצה.

steps.title: Why checking before the window makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's words and grants that checking before the window is useful, because hairs found then show that later hairs are only a mole. This prepares a question about checking after the window.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהודה says, before the age window and after the age window women check them. Granted, before the window checking is needed, because if hairs are found after the window, they are a mole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to question רבי יהודה's ruling. It first agrees that checking before the window has a purpose, and it is getting ready to ask why anyone would need to check after the window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hairs that grew before the window do not count as a sign. If women saw them early, those hairs will not be mistaken for a real sign later, because they are treated like a mole. The "granted" (בשלמא) sets up a contrast: the purpose of checking after the window is not yet clear.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted: accepts one part before challenging another
A mole: hairs that grew too early, which do not count as a sign of maturity

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Before the age window and after the age window
women check them.
Granted, before the age window
checking is needed,
because if they are found after the age window
they are a mole.
phrases.notes: He means the same hairs the women already saw before the window. Those count only as a mole, not a sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לִפְנֵי הַפֶּרֶק בָּעֵי בְּדִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא ends, the גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה's view from step 13 and starts to analyze it
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that women check after the age window
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא grants a clear purpose for checking before the window: early hairs are marked as a mole. This sets up the question of what purpose checking after the window could serve.

steps.title: Why check after the age window at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a check is needed after the age window, since רבא says a girl who reached full age is presumed to have grown signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But after the age window, why do we need a check? רבא said that a girl who reached her full years needs no check, because we presume she has grown signs!
steps.whatsHappening: Step 17 said checking before the window makes sense. Now the גמרא attacks the other half of רבי יהודה's ruling: checking after the window seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא rules that once a girl reaches twelve years and a day, we presume she has grown the two hairs. If so, examining her then adds nothing. That clashes with רבי יהודה, who lets women check after the window.

keyTerms.meaning: After the age window (from twelve years and a day)
A physical check for signs of maturity
Her full years, the age of adulthood
A presumption we rely on without checking

phrases.english: But after the age window,
why do I need a check?
But didn't רבא say:
A minor girl who reached her full years
phrases.notes: He means twelve years and one day.

phrases.english: does not need a check,
there is a presumption that she has grown signs!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְאַחַר הַפֶּרֶק, לְמָה לִי בְּדִיקָה? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question set up in step 17 by turning to the after-the-window case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that women check a girl after the age window
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's presumption makes a check after the window pointless, so why does רבי יהודה call for one?

steps.title: רבא's presumption works for refusal, not for חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא's presumption is enough to stop her from doing מיאון, but for חליצה she still needs a real check.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבא spoke of the presumption, he meant it for מיאון. But for חליצה she needs a check.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by limiting רבא's rule to one area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stopping מיאון is a strict result, so a presumption is good enough. Allowing חליצה needs real proof that she is an adult. So a check after the window still has a job: it lets her do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor girl's refusal that ends a rabbinic marriage
The ceremony that frees a widow from יבום; it needs an adult

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא's presumption makes her a full adult for everything. It only stops her from refusing; for חליצה we still check.

phrases.english: When רבא spoke of the presumption, it was for refusal,
but for חליצה she needs a check.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמַר רָבָא חֲזָקָה לְמֵיאוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבא's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's presumption settles adulthood for every purpose, so checking is useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The presumption only blocks מיאון; חליצה still requires a check.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the window counts like adulthood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's words that women do not check during the window and explains that he treats the window like the time after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: During the window, women do not check them. He holds that during the window is like after the window.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of רבי יהודה's ruling and gives his reason. This sets up the next step, which explains how 'during' still differs from 'after'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, hairs found during the window count as real signs, making her an adult. That can lead to a lenient result (allowing חליצה), so women alone are not trusted then.

keyTerms.meaning: During the age window (eleven years and a day to twelve years and a day)

phrases.english: During the window
women do not check them,
He holds:
during the window is like after the window (it is similar).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the meaning is the same either way.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹךְ הַפֶּרֶק אֵין נָשִׁים בּוֹדְקוֹת אוֹתָן, קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the after-the-window case to the during-the-window case in רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, hairs during the window count as real signs, so women may not check then.

steps.title: Why women are trusted after the window but not during it
steps.stepSummary: After the window, רבא's presumption backs up the women's report, so we rely on them. During the window there is no such presumption, so we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the window, where רבא's presumption exists, we rely on women and they check. During the window, where רבא's presumption does not exist, we do not rely on women and women do not check.
steps.whatsHappening: If the window is just like adulthood, why treat the two times differently? The גמרא answers: after the window, רבא's presumption supports the women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After twelve, the women's check only confirms what we already presume, so it is easy to trust them. During the window, the women would be the only thing making her an adult, and that is too much to rest on them.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, women can check after the window because רבא's presumption backs them up. During the window there is no backup, so they cannot.

phrases.english: And after the window,
where there is רבא's presumption,
we rely on women and they check.
phrases.notes: אַנָּשִׁים here means 'on women' (אַ + נָשִׁים), not 'men'.

phrases.english: During the window,
where there is no presumption of רבא,
we do not rely on women,
and women do not check.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַחַר הַפֶּרֶק, דְּאִיכָּא חֲזָקָה דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question raised by step 20: if 'during' equals 'after', why the different rule?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a supporting presumption present in one case only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the window is treated like adulthood, women should be trusted then just as after it.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the window רבא's presumption supports the women; during it nothing does, so they are not relied on.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the window counts like childhood
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון lets women check during the window because he treats it like the time before it. The check only serves to mark those hairs as a mole if they are found again later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: even during the window women check them. He holds that during the window is like before the window, and she needs a check so that if the hairs are found after the window, they are a mole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי שמעון's side of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, hairs during the window do not make her an adult, so the women's report cannot lead to a lenient result. Its only effect is strict: hairs seen now are later treated as a mole and not as a sign.

keyTerms.meaning: A mole; hair growing from it is not a sign of maturity

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה treats the window like adulthood, so women can't check then. רבי שמעון treats it like childhood, so women can check, and the check only works strictly.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
even during the window,
women check them.
He holds:
during the window is like before the window,
and she needs a check
so that if they are found after the window,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the same hairs the women already saw during the window.

phrases.english: they are a mole.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף תּוֹךְ הַפֶּרֶק, נָשִׁים בּוֹדְקוֹת אוֹתָן. קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רבי יהודה to explaining the opposing view of רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי שמעון, the window is like childhood, so women may check then; their check only marks the hairs as a mole.

steps.title: A woman is believed only to be stringent
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that a woman who checks the girl is believed if her report leads to a stricter ruling, but not if it leads to a more lenient one.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman is believed to make things stricter, but not to make things more lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more line from the same ברייתא. It is about how far we trust a woman who checks the girl for signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line already appeared in the ברייתא (step 14). The גמרא now quotes it again in order to ask whose view it is. Her report counts only when it leads to a stricter result, not when it leads to a more lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: She is believed (her report is trusted)
To be stringent, leading to a stricter ruling
To be lenient, leading to a more permissive ruling

phrases.english: And a woman is believed to be stringent,
phrases.notes: This is still the same ברייתא the גמרא has been working through. The woman is the one who checked the girl.

phrases.english: but not to be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֶאֱמֶנֶת אִשָּׁה לְהַחְמִיר, אֲבָל לֹא לְהָקֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא after the opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון were explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's report about the girl's signs counts only when it leads to a stricter ruling.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that a woman is believed only to be stringent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one who teaches this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view this line follows. Neither opinion explained so far seems to match it neatly. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says women do not check during the window. רבי שמעון says they may check. A rule that trusts her only one way, for stringency, does not clearly fit either one, so the גמרא needs to place it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who teaches this? (asking which תנא is the author)

phrases.english: Who teaches this?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא, רבי יהודה or רבי שמעון, and in which time period, fits the rule that a woman is believed only to be stringent.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, talking about the age window
steps.stepSummary: One possible answer is that the line follows רבי יהודה and is talking about the age window.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is רבי יהודה, and it is talking about the time within the age window.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the line can follow רבי יהודה, as long as it is talking about the age window. The opening words mean 'if you want, say', which hints that another answer may follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said women do not check during the window. This line explains what that means: her report cannot be used to be lenient. But if her report leads to a stricter result, we still take it seriously. This fits his view that the window is treated like the time after it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: one possible answer, often followed by another
Within the age window (from 11 years and a day to 12 years and a day)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה changed his mind and now lets women check during the window. Her report still cannot help to be lenient. It only counts when it leads to a stricter result.

phrases.english: If you want, say: it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and it is talking about during the age window.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְאַתּוֹךְ הַפֶּרֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who the author is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule follows רבי יהודה and refers to the age window. There, her report cannot be used to be lenient, but it counts when it leads to a stricter result.
